newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE BUILDING SOCIETY LOWERS MORTGAGE RATES.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE BUILDING SOCIETY LOWERS MORTGAGE RATES.

text.p: Zimbabwe's largest building society, the Central Africa Building Society (CABS), has lowered its interest rates on mortgages by between 0.25 percent and 4.25 percent, citing falling money market rates.

The bank said in a statement the cuts, which are effective from April 1, also followed a reduction by the government last week in the rate of dividend payable on tax-free paid-up permanent shares to 15.25 percent from 18 percent.

It said it had reduced to 17.25 percent from 19 percent rates on residential mortgages of more than Z$45,000 while loans for new housing development would now attract a rate of 23 percent, slightly down from 23.5 percent.
Industrial loans in excess of Z$2.5 million, all commercial loans and loans to people who own second homes would now pay an interest rate of 24 percent versus 26.5 percent previously.

"The new reduced interest rates will give relief to all the Society's mortgagors' in the residential, commercial and industrial sectors," CABS senior deputy general manager Ambrose Matika said in the statement.
He said these mortgagors' loans exceeded Z$2 billion for the first time at the end of February.
